claims: PCSX2's PINE protocol defines guest memory read opcodes MsgRead8=0, MsgRead16=1, MsgRead32=2, MsgRead64=3 in pcsx2/PINE.cpp.
The headless PINE helper currently exposes only identity/save/load, not memory reads.
PINE can read guest EE memory without writing any guest state.
args.evidence: pcsx2/PINE.cpp enum IPCCommand: MsgRead8=0, MsgRead16=1, MsgRead32=2, MsgRead64=3, MsgWrite8=4, MsgWrite16=5, MsgWrite32=6, MsgWrite64=7; then Version=8, SaveState=9, LoadState=10, Title=11, Id=12, UUID=13, GameVersion=14, Status=15. The read handler replies with the value in a little-endian span. The headless helper tools/headless-runtime/pine_control.py implements only identity (text 8/11/12/13/14 + status 15) and save/load (9/10).
